q:
There were periods when neither of us slept for more than 1-2 hours at a time. Days and nights blended together and sometimes it felt like we were just trying to survive until the next nap.

What helped us the most wasn't a miracle sleep trick. It was having some structure. We started tracking sleep, feedings, wake windows and trying to understand our son's patterns.
cx: Father of an 18-month-old; he later names a tracking app he built.

q: In our case, we realized my wife wasn't producing enough milk, so we started supplementing with formula, and things gradually got better.
My husband and I would take shifts so that I could get 3-4h of sleep from 7-11pm and then I would take over the rest of the night and was awake as she slept on me...
r: safe sleep (baby sleeping on parent overnight)

q: July 18 (currently tonight): SHE FELL ASLEEP IN 2 MINUTES. […] I feel like I have my life back and my sleep anxiety has decreased SUBSTANTIALLY.
cx: Fourth night of sleep training at four months.

q: the one I followed from taking Cara babies was you don’t feed unless asleep
cx: Names the sleep course she followed.

q: He woke up at 12.30 am and 5 am for feeds. After we put him down, he fussed didn’t cry and fell asleep within less than 5 minutes. I was SHOOK!! […] Ofcourse I didn’t sleep because I was looking at the monitor all night like a crazy person lol.
cx: Night one of sleep training a six-month-old.

q: It’s just so heartbreaking but my husband keeps reminding me that we are helping him get his much needed sleep and rest for his development. That makes me feel less guilty but it’s so hard
cx: How her husband talks her through sleep training.

q: My baby had silent reflux so he was up every other hour, I legit thought I was gonna die of lack of sleep.
cx: Looking back at three months on the first weeks.

q: Bc no I didn’t enjoy my newborn bubble and it felt wrong. I literally was escaping to target every day without my kid lol.
cx: Her honest note to other mothers.

q: Now for the best part! We are sleeping through the night, but before he was only having one wake up at 2am. But everything is just so much easier now.
cx: At three months the baby sleeps through.

q: At around 6 months, things started going very downhill. She might wake up 9 times a night and would require very strenuous bouncing to go back to sleep. I was losing my mind.
cx: Breastfed baby bounced to sleep on an exercise ball.

q: It’s such a relief being able to get some sleep and have a bit of freedom in the evenings (no longer needing to rush to sleep after her because I couldn’t afford to waste any time I could be sleeping).
cx: Two months after a gentle pick-up-put-down method.

q: You will be sleep-deprived, but guess what, it's normal. 2-3 hours of sleep is normal. Feeding during those wake hours is NORMAL.
cx: First-time mother's advice ten days after birth.

q: And sleep, sleep, sleep as the baby naps.
cx: The sleep-when-baby-sleeps advice, from a mother ten days in.

q: We recently did Ferber for a week with our 8 month old baby. It went really well and I started sleeping again for the first time since she was born! (If you're on the fence about sleep training, it is a relief to not do 5-6 wake ups a night. Plus, you get to sleep more too).
cx: Opening of a schedule question after sleep training.

q: PLS and Huckleberry both recommend FAR shorter WW timings for 8 month olds. Am I just extending this far too long?
cx: Comparing a book and an app with her own schedule.
